summary: ZeroTier offline timer bug fix verified. Backend starts correctly with updated zerotier_alerts.py. All 14 backend tests passed (100%). ZeroTier alert scheduler runs every 60 seconds. The _check_alerts function now correctly implements offline_since timer logic: (1) Records offline_since timestamp when client first goes offline, (2) Only sends notification after 5+ minutes confirmed offline, (3) Sends recovery notification when client comes back online and clears timer.

minor.issue: Returns 400 'ZeroTier not configured' - this is expected behavior when API token/network_id not set for the site

critical_code_review_comments: zerotier_alerts.py line 53: OFFLINE_ALERT_DELAY_SECONDS = 300 (5 minutes) - correctly configured
zerotier_alerts.py lines 152-157: When client goes offline, offline_since timestamp is recorded and 5min timer starts
zerotier_alerts.py lines 159-201: Alert only sent after offline_duration >= OFFLINE_ALERT_DELAY_SECONDS (300s), then offline_alert_sent=True
zerotier_alerts.py lines 203-249: When client comes back online, recovery notification sent, offline_since cleared to None, offline_alert_sent reset to False
zerotier_alerts.py line 495: Scheduler loop sleeps 60 seconds between checks
zerotier_alerts.py line 523: Startup log confirms '60s interval'
context_for_next_testing_agent: ZeroTier offline timer bug fix verified. Key changes in zerotier_alerts.py: (1) New fields on zerotier_alerts documents: offline_since (ISO timestamp), offline_alert_sent (boolean), (2) OFFLINE_ALERT_DELAY_SECONDS = 300 (5 minutes), (3) Scheduler runs every 60 seconds. The fix ensures notifications are only sent after 5+ minutes confirmed offline, preventing false alerts for brief network blips. Recovery notifications are sent when clients come back online. Test site: db23c31a-7776-4805-a4a5-bd019dd7c2be has 9 alert configs but ZeroTier API token may not be configured (members endpoint returns 400).
